_comment: Narrow exemptions for the privacy scanner. Each entry names ONE literal and the EXACT files it may appear in. There is deliberately no wildcard: an allowlist that can be applied loosely stops being a decision and becomes a hole. Add an entry only when the value is already public by the owner's own choice AND the file cannot do its job without it.

allow.reason: The repository owner's GitHub handle. It is already public as the repository path itself, and a plugin marketplace manifest cannot omit the owner. This exempts the handle only; the full email address it is a local-part of remains blocked everywhere, including in these same files.

Quoted in a comment explaining a real defect: an unanchored match for the forename fired inside the word 'Jonathan'. The value IS the finding -- removing it destroys the explanation of why the pattern is anchored.
Quoted in a comment explaining why email LOCAL-PARTS are indexed as terms in their own right. The full address remains blocked everywhere including here.
Same comment as 'scholyx': the pair illustrates that a local-part leaks without its domain. The full address remains blocked.
Quoted in a comment explaining why concatenated forms of the name are matched. The full address remains blocked.
